unsupported_claims: Spectral methods such as Laplacian eigenmaps appear in the node2vec paper as related-work baselines. The evidence names only Spectral Clustering as a benchmark and never mentions Laplacian eigenmaps.
rationale: The answer correctly rejects the false premise, since the evidence lists Spectral Clustering only as a benchmark compared against node2vec, and it correctly describes the Wikipedia word co-occurrence network with POS-tag labels used for multilabel classification. Its description of the random-walk method (p/q parameters, skip-gram) is general knowledge of the node2vec method rather than something the excerpts spell out, and its mention of Laplacian eigenmaps goes beyond the evidence.
